summary.title: Calendar Versioning
summary.one_liner: CalVer is a versioning convention that encodes a project's release date in its version number, and this spec explains the date tokens, when to use it, and how to handle padding and multiple daily releases.
takeaways: CalVer uses release dates as version segments, such as YYYY.MINOR.MICRO or YY.0M, with tokens like YYYY, YY, 0M, M, 0D, and D.

Choose CalVer when a project has a large or fast-changing scope, time-sensitive updates, or non-technical audiences; use a changelog and deprecation policy since CalVer does not signal breaking changes.
Padding decisions matter: unpadded is the default for SemVer compatibility, while zero-padding helps when versions appear as sorted filenames or container tags.
For multiple releases in one day, append an incrementing micro segment such as 2026.9.11.1.
summary.summary: The page is a specification and guide for Calendar Versioning (CalVer), defining version segments and date tokens (YYYY, YY, 0M, M, 0W, W, 0D, D) and explaining the notation with examples. It walks through case studies of projects using CalVer, including Ubuntu, Apple, NVIDIA, Twisted, and yt-dlp, and lists other notable users. It also covers FAQs on when to adopt CalVer, handling breaking changes, multiple releases per day, and zero-padding trade-offs, plus a spec changelog and guidance on README badges.
